intro: Russia is an energy superpower, with huge reserves of oil and gas as well as metals, diamonds, timber and wheat. Since 2022 sanctions and war spending have reshaped its economy.

chapters.title: Oil and gas
text: Russia has the world's largest natural gas reserves and is one of the biggest oil producers. For decades pipelines carried its gas to Europe, which depended heavily on it.
After the invasion of Ukraine, Europe cut most of its purchases, and Russia now sells much more oil and gas to China, India and Turkey, often at discounted prices.

chapters.title: Wheat, metals and diamonds
text: Russia is the world's largest exporter of wheat, grown on the fertile black soils of the south. It is also a leading producer of nickel, palladium, aluminium, timber and diamonds; its company Alrosa mines more diamonds than any other.
It sells nuclear power stations abroad and launches astronauts and satellites on Soyuz rockets.

chapters.title: Challenges
text: Much of Russia's wealth is controlled by the state and a small number of oligarchs, and corruption is widespread. Sanctions have cut access to Western technology and finance, and since 2022 a large share of government spending has gone to the military. The currency is the rouble.

keyTerms.meaning: The amount of oil, gas or minerals known to be in the ground and possible to extract.
